newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk prosecutor asks Egypt to probe Erbakan story.
newsitem.headline: Turk prosecutor asks Egypt to probe Erbakan story.

text.p: Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is under investigation for alleged anti-secularist remarks in a case that could force closure of his ruling Welfare Party, according to court documents.

A written request from the Appeals Court, obtained by Reuters on Thursday, asks judicial authorities in Egypt to question a Cairo-based reporter on alleged anti-secularist remarks by Erbakan, then an opposition leader.
It said the comments were made to a journalist it identifed as Ali Iliva and described as the Cairo correspondent for the Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Anba.
"This interview...is against the law on political parties...and is a cause for the closure of a party," said the court's request, sent to Egypt last month.
A prosecutor told Reuters any information from Egypt would be passed to the Constitutional Court, dominated by secularists, which would consider banning Welfare.
The Turkish press has quoted Erbakan, who became modern Turkey's first Islamist leader in 1996, as telling the Kuwaiti newspaper that Turkey's secular system had caused poverty and backwardness.
Erbakan is alleged to have accused late national hero Kemal Ataturk of declaring war on Islam. Turkish law forbids strong criticism of Ataturk and statements regarded as promoting Islamist militancy.
Another court dropped a case against Erbakan in January for the same interview because its contents could not be checked, the prosecutor said.
Erbakan won a narrow victory in 1995 elections and became prime minister last year in coalition with secular conservatives.
